brief:
Middle East Eye published an account by Bahzad al Akhras, a Gaza resident, describing the destruction of his family's house as fundamentally different from losing physical structures or possessions. He characterized the loss as an erasure of a place that once contained his family's lived experience and memories.

Al Akhras's reflection raises the broader question of whether return is feasible for Palestinians whose homes were destroyed during the conflict. His account underscores how displacement in Gaza extends beyond housing shortages to encompass the loss of spaces tied to family identity and personal history.

The piece reflects experiences shared among many Gaza residents confronting reconstruction challenges and uncertainty about whether their former homes and communities can be rebuilt or reclaimed.
dek: After Israel's annihilation of Gaza, can I ever return home? Submitted by Bahzad al Akhras on Wed, 08/12/2026 - 17:30 The destruction of my family's house was not simply a loss of walls or furniture. It was the erasure of a place that once held our lives…
title: Gazan resident questions ability to return after family home destroyed
